meta.Zones covered: Lawns, gazebo & hedge beds | lake open water | algal channel & banks
meta.Annotated videos: Three MP4 files in this folder, one per clip

headlineFindings: The water bodies are the defining problem, exactly as recorded on site. Two thirds of this survey is water and both bodies are in poor condition: the algae channel peaks at 93.1% algae cover of its water surface, and the open lake peaks at 64.1%.

Floating waste is the single largest defect signal in the survey - 977 records, by far the highest of any park in the programme. It is spread across the open lake surface and concentrated along the algae channel.
Cleanliness is the worst indicator: 34.9 on the algae channel and 37.2 on the lake. Both are the lowest cleanliness scores recorded at any park except the Sanjay Lake construction zone.
Bank condition is poor. 328 exposed-bed / bank-erosion records along the stone-lined channel and lake margins, with bare dry ground running right up to the water edge on both sides.
The lawn and gazebo zone is the least-bad part of the park at 75.7 overall, but still carries 15% bare ground and 56.1 cleanliness. The gazebo itself is visible and weathered.
Green cover is present but patchy - lawn runs 10.7-19.8% across the three zones with bare ground at 12-16%.
facilities sits at 71-77 across all zones, the weakest facilities spread of any park surveyed.

recommendations.Finding: Both water bodies are severely degraded. The channel is choked with a dense algae and weed mat covering up to 93% of its surface; the open lake peaks at 64% algae cover and carries the highest floating-waste count in the whole programme (977 records).
recommendations.Recommended action: Commission a water-body restoration programme as the park's top priority: mechanical weed and algae removal, de-silting, nutrient and inflow control, and aeration. Investigate the inflow - this degree of eutrophication indicates a continuing nutrient or sewage load, not a one-off.

recommendations.Finding: The site record notes exposed electric wires laid in the open, utility damage and an unsafe bridge. None of these is detectable from RGB drone imagery at survey altitude, so the report cannot measure them - but an exposed live conductor in a public park is a life-safety issue.
recommendations.Recommended action: Commission an immediate ground safety inspection covering electrical services, the bridge structure and any open utility. Do not wait on drone evidence for this - the technology cannot see it.

recommendations.Finding: Floating waste is spread across the lake surface and concentrated along the channel; ground debris drives cleanliness to 34.9 on the channel zone.
recommendations.Recommended action: Deploy surface skimming and net booms on both water bodies, run a shoreline clearance drive, and increase bin provision and emptying around the water edge where the waste originates.

recommendations.Finding: 328 bank-erosion records along stone-lined margins, with bare dry ground running to the water edge on both sides.
recommendations.Recommended action: Stabilise and re-profile the eroded banks; establish a vegetated buffer strip to reduce runoff and silt entering the water.

recommendations.Finding: Green cover is patchy park-wide - lawn 10.7-19.8% with bare ground at 12-16%.
recommendations.Recommended action: Reinstate ground cover on the bare areas, prioritising the strip between the paths and the water edge where erosion feeds the water body.

recommendations.Finding: facilities sits at 71-77 across all zones - the weakest spread of any park surveyed. Only 126 pathway and 96 bench records, and the gazebo is visibly weathered.
recommendations.Recommended action: Survey the path network and built assets; the low detection counts suggest a fragmented and under-maintained network rather than a detector limitation.

recommendations.Finding: Several items on the site record are simply not in these three clips: the bridge, children's rides, the water fountain, the main gate, excavation tools and streetlights.
recommendations.Recommended action: Fly those specific features. The current three clips are weighted heavily toward the water bodies and under-represent the built assets that the site record flags as poor.

recommendations.Finding: No class exists for: exposed wires, utility damage, bridge condition, gazebo condition, roof-surface garbage, streetlights, main gate, water pipes, or 'broken' as a state.
recommendations.Recommended action: Several of these are the defects that matter most at this park. Vertical-surface and thin-linear-feature detection is a materially different problem from the ground-plane work done so far.

recommendations.Finding: No .SRT telemetry accompanied these clips, and this is a single-date capture.
recommendations.Recommended action: Export flight logs with the video to unlock geo-tagging and the issue map; repeat the flight path later for change detection against this baseline.
